correctness.rationale: For each majority-stable \(S\), the tournament arc count \(s(s-1)/2\le s\lfloor(n-1)/4\rfloor\) gives \(s\le2k+1\). Explicit parity-residue \(S\) of size \(2k+1\) has exactly \(k\) internal outneighbours at every vertex, including \(n=3\). Cyclic translations form feasible fractional weights of \(1/(2k+1)\) with exact vertex coverage one, matching the universal lower bound. Explicit partitions prove the ordinary two-/three-colour bounds. Exhaustive checks cover 174760 subsets through \(n=17\), direct LP solutions through \(n=13\), and 250 odd orders through \(n=501\), but the mathematical proof establishes the infinite claim.

value.rationale: The theorem completely calculates a natural fractional graph/digraph invariant in every order of an infinite vertex-transitive tournament family, with matching explicit primal and counting-dual witnesses. Alternating values above/below two and sharp integer two/three parity transitions give non-obvious structural benchmarks for fractional majority colouring, beyond general uniform bounds.
